title: Choose table image

title: Auto Corners

title: Open or close Fine Tune Corner

title: Reset Corners

title: Choose analysis rack type

title: Analyze Balls

title: Add Missed Ball

title: AI detector mode and readiness

narration: This control selects the trained ball detector and shows its readiness. Loading means the model is being prepared. Ready means it can be used. Off uses the alternative detector, and Retry attempts to load the model again.

title: Practice pathway

Count pocketing, cue ball position, and legal contact separately. Your score should show what improved and what still needs work.

title: Speed and contact baseline
narration: Begin with a straight shot and center cue tip contact. Find the speed that produces a stop shot, then move the contact point higher for follow and lower for draw. Keep the object ball and pocket fixed while changing one setting at a time. Next, use a cut shot to compare the tangent line with the cue ball route. Before each shot, name the landing point you expect. Repeat each setup five times and record whether the cue ball finished short, long, left, or right.

title: Target landing precision
narration: Set up a repeatable object ball shot and choose a small cue ball landing zone. Begin with a generous target, then reduce it as your control improves. For this practice plan, use a three inch target and count a success only when the object ball is pocketed and the cue ball center finishes inside the target. Shoot ten attempts. Change only speed, then contact height, then the cut angle. Aim for eight successes out of ten before making the target smaller. Open More for Dr. Dave’s target practice demonstration.

title: Rock Around the Clock
narration: Open More and use Niels Feijen’s demonstration to set up Rock Around the Clock. Save the starting layout. Before every shot, choose the next object ball, its pocket, and the cue ball landing zone that leaves a useful angle. Prefer a route with room for a small speed error. Track pocketing and position separately. Complete one rotation first, then work toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. When you miss position, repeat the previous shot and compare a simpler route before changing the whole pattern.

title: One-rail kick reference
narration: Place an object ball behind a blocker so the cue ball needs one cushion to reach it. Open More for the diamond system tutorial. Identify the cue ball start, the rail aim point, and the intended object ball contact. Keep speed and spin consistent while testing the route. Repeat five attempts, moving the rail aim point by a small amount when the contact misses. Record the adjustment that works, then test a second starting location. Count legal object ball contact according to the game you are practicing.

title: Two-rail kick extension
narration: Begin with a two cushion route that has space for the cue ball to travel. Mark the first rail aim point and predict the second rail contact before shooting. Keep the same speed and spin for each attempt. If the first contact is wrong, adjust the aim point. If the first contact is right but the final contact misses, examine the second rail route and speed. Record five attempts from the same start, then move the cue ball to a new starting diamond. Open More for the linked kick reference.

title: Corner-5 three-rail route
narration: Open More for Dr. Dave’s Corner-5 demonstration. Follow its starting, aiming, and arrival number scales together. Identify all three cushion contacts before you shoot. Start with a clear route, consistent speed, and the spin shown in the lesson. Compare the predicted arrival with the actual arrival, then make a small adjustment and repeat. Once the route is calibrated, add a target object ball and a blocker for escape practice. Test five different starting positions and record legal object ball contact separately from the final cue ball position.

title: Progressive difficulty benchmark
narration: Open More for Sharivari’s progressive difficulty drill and use the demonstrated setup. Save the starting layout and record your first score. For your Trainer adaptation, begin with a comfortable position zone. After a successful set, reduce the zone or increase the shot difficulty, changing one condition at a time. Count both the pocketed ball and the required cue ball position. If the same error repeats, return to the last successful level. Record the highest level you can repeat, rather than only your best isolated attempt.

title: 105-minute practice session
narration: Use this one hundred and five minute practice plan. Spend thirty minutes on speed and target landing, aiming for eight successful pocket and position results out of ten with a three inch target. Spend forty five minutes on Rock Around the Clock, first completing one rotation and then working toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. Spend thirty minutes on kick escapes, starting with one rail and adding two and three rails as control improves. Test five selected escapes and aim for four legal contacts. Record the result at the end of each phase. If time runs out, save your layout and score, then continue there next session.

title: Review, save, and repeat
narration: At the end of practice, record attempts, pocketed balls, successful position results, and legal kick contacts. Note the most common miss and the single adjustment that helped. Save the table with a name that includes the drill, difficulty, and date. Download its table file if you want to share the same layout with an instructor or student. Begin your next session with that saved layout and the same scoring conditions. Improve the weakest result first, then increase the challenge once you can repeat the improvement.

title: Stop Shot Calibration
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Cue Ball Control > Stop Shot Calibration
narration: Stop Shot Calibration. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot end. Place the 1-ball on the center spot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the left long rail. This lines up with the foot-right corner pocket. Center a three-inch white circle one ball width behind the 1-ball, toward the cue ball. That is the cue ball’s stopping position. Use no side spin. Start slightly below center and adjust your speed and tip height until the cue ball arrives without forward or backward roll. Pocket the 1-ball and stop the cue ball inside the white circle. Reset both balls after each attempt. Try five shots and count clean stops. In the Trainer, select Execute Shot to watch the result.

title: 90-Degree Stun Tangent Line
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Cue Ball Control > 90-Degree Stun Tangent Line
narration: Ninety-Degree Stun Tangent Line. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the table’s center line, half a diamond toward the foot end from the center spot. Place a three-inch yellow square one and a half diamonds toward the head end from the 1-ball, and one ball width to its left. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Use no side spin and enough low tip contact and speed for the cue ball to be sliding at impact. It should leave along the tangent line, perpendicular to the object ball’s path. Adjust speed to finish inside the yellow square. Reset both balls and repeat five times. Select Execute Shot in the Trainer to compare the path with the tangent line.

title: Speed Ladder — Four Zones
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Cue Ball Control > Speed Ladder — Four Zones
narration: Speed Ladder. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Use only the cue ball. Start on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Place four three-inch circles on the center line: white on the center spot, red on the foot spot, yellow one diamond from the foot cushion, and pink one diamond from the head cushion. Reset the cue ball to the same starting position before every shot. First, stop on white. Second, stop on red. Third, touch the foot cushion and return to yellow. Fourth, touch the foot cushion and return all the way to pink. Use a level cue and no side spin. Change your stroke speed while keeping your delivery smooth. Score one point for each finish inside its circle, for a maximum of four. Repeat the ladder and compare your scores.

title: L-Drill — Five-Ball Rotation
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Positional Patterns > L-Drill — Five-Ball Rotation
narration: The L-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place balls one, two, and three half a diamond from the right long rail, respectively one, two, and three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place ball four one diamond from the right long rail and half a diamond from the foot cushion. Place ball five on the center line, also half a diamond from the foot cushion. These five balls form an L. Put a white square at the center spot, one diamond wide. Start the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond behind the head string. Pocket balls one through five in order, choosing clear corner pockets. Plan the next angle before every shot. Use the center square as a recovery option when it helps the next shot. Count balls pocketed in sequence, then reset the full pattern and try again.

title: T-Drill — Center and Foot String
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Positional Patterns > T-Drill — Center and Foot String
narration: The T-Drill. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place ball one on the center spot. Place ball two one diamond farther toward the foot, and ball three on the foot spot. Put ball four on the foot string, one diamond to the left of ball three, and ball five one diamond to its right. Start the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place two yellow circles, each half a diamond wide, halfway between the center spot and the side pockets. Pocket balls one through five in order into corner pockets. Choose the yellow zone that gives you a useful angle for the next ball. Use a cushion when it helps the route. Keep the cue ball clear of the remaining balls. Count your run, reset the full pattern, and work toward completing all five.

title: Wagon Wheel — Six Target Zones
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Positional Patterns > Wagon Wheel — Six Target Zones
narration: The Wagon Wheel. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond inward from the right side pocket. Put the cue ball on the center line, half a diamond toward the foot from the center spot. Set six three-inch circles on the head side of the 1-ball. Marker one is one and a half diamonds from the left rail and three and a half from the head rail. Marker two is two from the left and three from the head. Marker three is one ball width left of the 1-ball’s line and three from the head. Marker four is three and a quarter from the left and three from the head. Marker five is three and a half from the left and two and a half from the head. Marker six is directly headward of marker three, one and a half diamonds from the head rail. Reset both balls before every attempt and pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Work through the markers in order, varying draw, follow, and speed. Start without side spin. Record the combinations that produce repeatable finishes.

title: Two-Rail Center Recovery
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Rail Navigation > Two-Rail Center Recovery
narration: Two-Rail Center Recovery. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball one diamond from the right long rail and one diamond from the foot cushion. Put the cue ball on the same rail offset, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the head cushion. Make the square one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the foot-right corner. Start with natural forward roll and no side spin. Look for the cue ball to contact the foot cushion, then the left long cushion, and travel toward the white recovery zone. Adjust your stroke speed to finish in the square. Keep the ball placements fixed so you can compare attempts. Score the pocketed ball and the position result separately. Try five shots, then repeat your most successful speed.

title: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Rail Navigation > Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance
narration: Side Pocket Scratch Avoidance. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the 1-ball half a diamond inward from the right side pocket. Start the cue ball on the foot spot. Place a red square beside the head-right corner pocket, centered a quarter diamond from each cushion. Make it half a diamond wide. Place a white square on the center line, one diamond from the foot cushion, and make it one diamond wide. Pocket the 1-ball into the right side pocket. Compare forward roll, stun, and controlled draw, starting without side spin. Watch the whole cue ball route, including any cushion rebounds. Find a stroke that keeps the cue ball clear of the red danger zone and returns it toward white. In the Trainer, judge whether the path enters the red zone, even if cue ball pocketing is prevented. Reset both balls and repeat five times.

title: One-Rail Mirror Kick
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Kicking Systems > One-Rail Mirror Kick
narration: One-Rail Mirror Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Put the cue ball on the head string, one diamond from the right long rail. Place the 1-ball on that same line, three diamonds from the foot cushion. Put the 8-ball halfway between them to block the direct shot. The cue ball and the 1-ball are now equally distant from the left cushion. Mark the left cushion halfway between their lengthwise positions: three and a half diamonds from the head cushion. Center a yellow circle one ball radius inside that cushion as the cue ball contact reference. Use a level cue, moderate speed, and no side spin. Send the cue ball to the left cushion, then into the 1-ball without touching the 8-ball first. Begin with the midpoint reference and make small aiming adjustments from your observed results. Reset the cue ball after each attempt and count five clean contacts.

title: Two-Rail Corner Kick
targets: Guide > More > Practice Drills > Kicking Systems > Two-Rail Corner Kick
narration: Two-Rail Corner Kick. Stand at the head end, looking toward the foot. Place the cue ball one diamond from the head cushion and one and a quarter diamonds from the right long rail. Put the 1-ball one diamond from the foot cushion and three quarters of a diamond from the right long rail. Place the 8-ball level with the side pockets, one diamond from the right rail. Put balls two and three on the same line, two ball widths to either side of the 8-ball toward the head and foot ends. This blocks the direct shot. Place yellow marker A at the right cushion on the foot string, with its center one ball radius inside the cloth. Place yellow marker B half a diamond left of the foot-right corner, also one ball radius inside the foot cushion. Use moderate speed and no side spin. Aim the cue ball center toward A. Look for right cushion, then foot cushion near B, then contact with the 1-ball. Make small aiming adjustments and count five successful escapes.
